“First count to ten,” said Mrs. Jewls.
Joe counted to ten: “six, eight, twelve, one, five, two, seven, eleven, three, ten.” “No, Joe, that is wrong,” said Mrs. Jewls.
“No, it isn’t,” said Joe. “I counted until I got to ten.” “But you were wrong,” said Mrs. Jewls. “I’ll prove it to you.” She put five pencils on his desk. “How many pencils do we have here, Joe?” Joe counted the pencils. “Four, six, one, nine, five. "Nothing’s easy for Joe," said Maurecia. "He’s stupid." "I can beat you up," said Joe.

"Try it," said Maurecia.

beats.action_pt: Close-up no rosto de Joe com a cabeça apoiada na carteira, olhos fechados, expressão de desespero e lágrimas prestes a cair, enquanto Mrs. Jewls aparece ao fundo colocando uma mão gentil no ombro de Joe.
beats.narration:
"Don’t feel bad, Joe," said Mrs. Jewls.

"I just don’t get it," said Joe. "I’ll never learn how to count." "Sure you will, Joe," said Mrs. Jewls. "One day it will just come to you. You’ll wake up one morning and suddenly be able to count." Joe asked, "If all I have to do is wake up, what am I going to school for?" "School just speeds things up," said Mrs. Jewls. "Without school it might take another seventy years before you wake up and are able to count." "By that time I may have no hair left on top of my head to count," said Joe.

"Exactly," said Mrs. Jewls. "That is why you go to school."
